sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties in this revision petition are referred to as per their status and rank before the Trial Court.

3. The brief facts of the case of prosecution are that on 05.01.2009, the accused approached the complainant and requested for financial assistance of Rs.5,00,000/- for purchase of property and for other domestic purpose.
After considering the request of accused, complainant had paid a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- to the accused through Cheque bearing No.833361 dated 06.01.2019 drawn on State Bank of Hyderabad.

The accused has encashed the said cheque and while borrowing the said hand loan, the accused promised to repay the same within one year and also agreed to pay the interest at Rs.5,000/- per month till repayment of the principal amount.
It is stated that the accused paid interest of Rs.5,000/- per month through Cheque till 23.03.2010 and thereafter the accused has not paid interest.

In the 1st week of June 2013, the complainant NC: 2024:KHC:2203 demanded for return of principal amount and interest and in order to repay the borrowed loan, the accused had issued a Cheque bearing No.111367 dated 27.06.2013 for Rs.5,00,000/- drawn on State Bank of India, Basavanagudi Branch, Bangalore in favour of the complainant and assured that the said Cheque will be honoured on its presentation.

As per the instructions of the accused, on 28.06.2013,
the complainant has presented the said Cheque through her banker viz., State Bank of Hyderabad,
Basavanagudi Branch, Bangalore for collection.
On 28.06.2013, the said Cheque was returned unpaid for the reason "Funds Insufficient".
Thereafter, notice was issued to the accused through RPAD to pay the Cheque amount.

The same was returned unserved with a shara "not claimed,
intimation dropped".
Hence, the complainant has lodged complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act.

5.

On closure of prosecution side evidence,
statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded and the accused has totally denied the evidence of prosecution witnesses and he has not chosen to lead any evidence on his behalf.

Having heard on both sides, the Trial Court has convicted the accused for the offence punishable under Section 138 of N.I. Act and sentenced to pay a fine of Rs.6,25,000/-, in default of payment of fine, he shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one year.

Out of the total fine amount, a sum of Rs.6,20,000/-
is ordered to be paid to the complainant by way of compensation under Section 357 of Cr.P.C. and the balance of Rs.5,000/- shall be NC: 2024:KHC:2203 remitted as fine to the State Government.

Being aggrieved by this judgment of conviction and order of sentence, the accused preferred an appeal in Criminal Appeal No.326/2017 before the LXVII Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge,
Bengaluru City (CCH No.68).

Both came to be dismissed by the First Appellate Court.
Being aggrieved by this judgment, the revision petitioner/accused has preferred this present revision petition.
6. Learned counsel of the revision petitioner submits that the Courts below have erred in noticing the fact that no statutory notice is served on the appellant prior to filing of the complaint.

The appellant was residing at No.67A, Rangarao Road Cross, Shankarapuram, Basavanagudi,
Bengaluru-560 004 from 2011-2014.

Prior to 2011, the appellant was residing at No.2/2015,
Sowrabha, 1st Road, North Public School Road, NC: 2024:KHC:2203 Basavanagudi, Bangalore.
The same is evident from the Bank Passbook - Ex.D5 and D6.
In order to prove the said fact, the revision petitioner has also produced Driving License, Extract of Driving License-Ex.D2, a Lease Agreement - Ex.D8.
The revision petitioner further examined Sri. B.P. Prasad, the owner of the said house.
Appellant has also produced the speed post letter issued from the RTO Office to the above said address to the revision petitioner.
However, the said postal address was not permitted to be marked by the Court.
These facts clearly go to show that no notice served to the accused prior to filing of the complaint, which is mandatory.
Hence, the impugned judgment passed by the Trial Court which is confirmed by the Appellate Court are liable to be set-aside.
Further, it is submitted that the notice is sent to the address of the appellant mentioned in the cause title.
The notice was issued on 05.07.2013.
The said notice was returned unserved with postal shara "Absent (I/D)" on 06.07.2013 and 08.07.2013.
Immediately, the notice is returned to the Office of the counsel for respondent on NC: 2024:KHC:2203 09.07.2013.

As per the postal manual, Volume 6/3 if intimation is given, the said Registered post has to be kept in deposit from the date of intimation or a complaint, the article should be returned to the sender after seven days, but

in the present case, though intimation is not delivered, respondent provided that the postal authority has made the shara "intimation delivered"
and returned the same to the respondent advocate within two days.
Hence, in the light of the fact that there was no service of summons, the Court below has erred in passing the impugned Order and the same are liable to be set-aside.

Further, it is submitted that the Cheque in question was not Sri S R Venkatesh Babu vs Padma Aswath Gupta on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147266328/

sentences.text: Apart from this, after issuing the summons, the accused appeared before the Trial Court and enlarged on bail and he has executed a bail bond Form No.45 in which he has clearly stated the address given in the cause title of the complaint.
This bail bond executed by the accused/revision petitioner and Ex.P8-copy of the revision petition filed by the accused clearly reveals that the accused was residing in the same address.
However, the accused has taken false defence.
Hence, the same cannot be accepted.
Both the courts have properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts.

13. On re-appreciation/ re-examination/ re- consideration of the entire evidence on record, I do not find any illegality/infirmity in the judgment of conviction - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:2203 passed by the Trial Court which is confirmed by the Appellate Court.
